tasks.gr11-measurement-t3: Topic: Measurement. Revise and apply measurement of 2D and 3D shapes — perimeter, area, surface area and volume — with emphasis on unit consistency and diagram interpretation. Cover conversions between units (e.g. cm² to m², mℓ to ℓ), formulae for prisms, cylinders, cones and spheres, and the link between measurement and geometry. Ask Grade 11 learners to select correct formulae, convert units correctly, and solve multi-step measurement problems in context.
tasks.gr11-euclidean-geometry-t3: Topic: Euclidean Geometry — Circle Theorems. Cover the main circle theorems: angle at centre = 2 × inscribed angle; angle in semicircle = 90°; angles in same segment are equal; opposite angles in cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary; tangent perpendicular to radius; tangent-chord angle equals inscribed angle in alternate segment; equal chords equidistant from centre; perpendicular from centre bisects chord. Ask Grade 11 learners to identify applicable theorems, write formal proofs with reasons, and solve riders involving tangents, chords and cyclic quadrilaterals.
tasks.gr11-trig-sine-cosine-rule-t3: Topic: Trigonometry — Sine Rule, Cosine Rule and Area Rule. Cover the sine rule (a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C), cosine rule (a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A), and area rule (Area = ½ab sin C) for non-right-angled triangles; identify when each rule applies; handle the ambiguous case; and solve two-dimensional problems involving bearing or elevation. Ask Grade 11 learners to select the correct rule, set up and solve triangle problems, and calculate areas with the area rule.
tasks.gr11-finance-growth-decay-t3: Topic: Finance, Growth and Decay. Cover compound growth A = P(1+i)^n and compound decay A = P(1−i)^n; straight-line (constant amount) vs reducing-balance (constant percentage) depreciation; converting between nominal and effective interest rates using the formula; and multi-step investment or depreciation questions involving timelines. Ask Grade 11 learners to distinguish growth from decay, apply the correct formula, convert interest rates, and compare financial options over time.
tasks.gr11-probability-t3: Topic: Probability. Cover dependent and independent events (P(A and B) = P(A)×P(B) for independent); the addition rule P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B); the complement rule P(A') = 1 − P(A); mutually exclusive events; and constructing and interpreting tree diagrams for multi-stage experiments. Ask Grade 11 learners to decide whether events are independent, calculate compound probabilities with and without replacement, draw tree diagrams, and apply complement and union rules correctly.
